newsitem.title: USA: NYH heating oil cargoes go begging despite cold.
newsitem.headline: NYH heating oil cargoes go begging despite cold.

text.p: U.S. spot heating oil prices continued their downhill roll Friday tracking futures, with several cargoes unable to find buyers in New York Harbor despite the coldest weather this year in the key Northeast market, traders said.
Players said at least four distillate cargoes en route to the East Coast have yet to be placed.

"These cargoes need homes but haven't found them yet," a distillate broker said, adding two were British Petroleum shipments from the Gulf Coast and another was from Vitol S.A.'s refinery in Come by Chance, Newfoundland.
Neither of the companies were immediately available for comment.
"The arb is not working out of the Gulf Coast" for exports to Europe, one trader said, complicating the difficulty of unloading ample barrels.
Another trader active in New York Harbor said many players were out of the market Friday ahead of the weekend, perhaps another obstacle for would-be sellers.

NYMEX traders bid February heat down over 0.65 cent a gallon by 1335 EST (1835 GMT) to 69.25 cents even as some East Coast residents traded complaints about single-digit or low-teen temperatures (Fahrenheit) seen in the early morning.
The slide came on the heels of Thursday's heating oil selloff that saw Feburary futures drop by 1.5 cents on the New York Mercantile Exchange.
And differentials on New York Harbor heat remained stalled Friday at about 0.25 cent over the February NYMEX print despite expectations of similarly cold weather over the weekend.
"With the exception of weather, there's just little support for heating oil," one New York player said, citing a litany of offsetting bearish factors.

Among them were forecasts of moderating temperatures by the middle of next week and new API inventory data showing East Coast stocks now within 3.2 million barrels of last year's levels -- just half the year-on-year shortfall cited week ago.
Meanwhile, a maximum stream of distillates continue to arrive into New York Harbor from the Gulf Coast via the Colonial Pipeline, which has extended allocations through the month of February.
